title: Acyclic Cartan--Eilenberg total cohomology and image filtration
statement: Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B,\mathcal C$ be Grothendieck abelian categories with derived categories and let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$, $G:\mathcal B\to\mathcal C$ be additive left exact functors such that $F$ sends injectives to $G$-acyclic objects [def-sp-composite-acyclicity]. Let $E:\mathcal A\to E_2\mathrm{SpectralSequence}(\mathcal C)$ be a functor, with an isomorphism $c_X$ from each $E(X)$ to the truncation spectral sequence of $RG(RF(X))$. For every presentation $P$ [def-sp-cartan-eilenberg-presentation], let $L_P$ be a filtration on $\operatorname{Tot}G(P.I)$ equal degreewise to the second filtration [def-sp-double-complex-total]. There exist isomorphisms $h_P^n:H^n(\operatorname{Tot}G(P.I))\cong R^n(GF)(P.X)$ natural for presentation comparisons, and decreasing filtrations $HF_X^n$ on $R^n(GF)(X)$. The augmentation of the mapped injective resolution into resolution-degree-zero total summands, using the canonical extension isomorphisms, induces the inverse of the canonical injective-resolution derived computation after composition with $h$. Each $HF_{P.X}^n(p)$ is the image of $H^n(L_P^p)\to H^n(\operatorname{Tot}G(P.I))\xrightarrow{h}R^n(GF)(P.X)$. For $p\ge0$ this step equals the transport through the canonical abutment isomorphism of the truncation image at $n+1-p$. Every filtration step is natural in $X$. For all $p,q\ge0$ and $r>\max(p,q+1)$ with $r\ge2$, the term $E_r^{p,q}(X)$ is isomorphic to $\operatorname{gr}^p HF_X^{p+q}$.

proof.text: The common augmentation, the extension isomorphisms and the degree-zero total inclusions define a cochain map a from GF(J) extended by zero. The bicomplex augmentation squares and total-complex signs verify its differential equation.

Columns compute derived G on F(J^i), which is acyclic by the hypothesis. Their positive rows vanish. The first-quadrant first spectral sequence collapses, so a induces homology isomorphisms. Define h by their inverses followed by the canonical resolution computation. Naturality of a and of that computation yields the comparison square and augmentation equation.

Transport the second image filtration through h. In total degree n, cycles of Dec(L)^(-q), q=n-p, are precisely total cycles lying in L^p. Thus the images in total cohomology coincide. Before applying G, the Dec filtration on Tot(I) is a filtered injective resolution of the canonical truncation filtration: horizontal cycle and boundary resolutions give the graded quasi-isomorphisms and injective terms give split degreewise filtrations. Left exact additive G preserves the kernels and finite sums defining Dec. Tag 015X therefore identifies Dec(L)^(-q) with RG(tau_{<=q} F(J)), compatibly with the maps into the full derived object. Hence its image is the canonical truncation image, independent of P. For p<0 the filtered complex is all of the total complex, so define HF on X using these canonical images and whole negative steps. Comparison maps give the stated step naturality.

Use the existing spectral-object page and quotient-image computations on the truncation spectral object: first-quadrant vanishing replaces the outer indices by bottom and top once r>max(p,q+1), while the short exact sequence of successive opcycle images identifies the resulting term with the quotient of image-filtration steps. The step equality from the preceding step transports this quotient through the canonical abutment isomorphism to the graded piece of HF. Compose with the page-r component of c_X. This uses only objectwise isomorphisms c_X, not naturality of c.
